reviewPolicy: 30-day monetary review window; expired or unreviewed records suppress estimates. A review date is not an enactment or effective date.
scope: Speeding only; program-specific rules. Not a complete statement of current traffic law.

sources.title: New York Senate · VTL §1180
sources.reviewNote: §1180(h)(1), (3), (5): ordinary/work-zone ranges and repeat-offense maximum increases. School-zone paragraph (4) is not modeled.

sources.title: New York State · Automated Work Zone Speed Enforcement
sources.reviewNote: First violation $50; second within 18 months $75; third and subsequent within 18 months $100. No license points; late fees can apply.

sources.title: New York Senate · VTL §1180-b
sources.reviewNote: Monetary liability shall not exceed fifty dollars for each violation; additional late penalty may apply. NYC program only. Source includes provisions taking effect in 2027; no future procedural provision is applied.

sources.title: Pennsylvania General Assembly · 75 Pa.C.S. §3362
sources.reviewNote: Base $42.50 when the maximum speed limit is 65 mph or higher; otherwise $35. Add $2 per mph exceeding five mph over the maximum.

sources.title: Pennsylvania General Assembly · 75 Pa.C.S. §3369
sources.reviewNote: First offense written warning; second $75; third and subsequent $150. A second or subsequent offense must occur at least 15 days after mailing of the warning. Active and in-use system required.

sources.title: Pennsylvania General Assembly · 75 Pa.C.S. §3326
sources.reviewNote: §3362 fines double in qualifying active work zones manned by workers, with required official signs. Other injury and license consequences are separate.

sources.title: Maryland General Assembly · Transportation §21-810
sources.reviewNote: 12–15 mph over $60; 16–19 $80; 20–29 $140; 30–39 $270; 40+ $500. Double these amounts when workers are present. This is not the schedule for other Maryland camera programs.

sources.title: Virginia Legislative Information System · §46.2-882.1
sources.reviewNote: At least 10 mph over; civil penalty shall not exceed $100. Work-zone liability requires workers present. A personally issued summons can carry different record consequences from a mailed notice. Page includes future 2027 provisions; those are not applied.

sources.title: Virginia Legislative Information System · §46.2-878.3
sources.reviewNote: Where prepayment is permitted: $6 per mph ordinary, $7 for specified school/work-zone offenses. Extra $100 for over 80 but below 86 on a 65 mph road. Other specified residential rules not modeled.

sources.title: Virginia Legislative Information System · §46.2-862
sources.reviewNote: Reckless-driving speed threshold: 20 mph or more above the limit, or over 85 mph regardless of limit.

sources.title: California Legislature · Vehicle Code §22426
sources.reviewNote: AB 645 pilot: 11–15 mph over $50; 16–25 $100; 26+ $200 unless actual speed is at least 100 mph, then $500. Civil penalty, no violation point.

sources.title: California Legislature · Vehicle Code §22425
sources.reviewNote: Six designated local jurisdictions only. Excludes interstates, state routes and other specified roads. Initial 60-day warning periods; vehicle’s first 11–15 mph violation in a jurisdiction is a warning. Income-based reductions available.

sources.title: New Jersey Courts · Published Statewide Violations Bureau Schedule
sources.reviewNote: Document is dated July 29, 2021. Retained as a dated source; not enabled for a current monetary calculation until superseding schedules and applicability are checked.

sources.title: New Jersey DOT · Red Light Running Pilot
sources.reviewNote: Agency reports that the former red-light pilot ended December 16, 2014. Historical camera lists do not establish present enforcement authority.

sources.title: DC Office of Documents · 18 DCMR §2600
sources.reviewNote: Current index lists an August 7, 2026 amendment. The adopted text was subsequently retrieved and verified as source dc-adopted; the earlier calculation hold has been resolved.

sources.title: Maine Legislature · 29-A §2074
sources.reviewNote: §2074(3-A): Maine Turnpike/interstate speeding under 30 mph over carries a statutory minimum $50. This is a floor, not the court fine schedule or an exact payable amount. 30+ mph over is a criminal matter under subsection 3.

sources.title: Maine Legislature · 29-A §2117
sources.reviewNote: Restricts state/municipal camera proof or enforcement of Title 29-A; statutory exceptions include school-bus and Turnpike toll enforcement. Those exceptions are not general speed-camera authority.

sources.title: New Hampshire General Court · RSA 265:60
sources.reviewNote: Paragraph V standard tiers: $50/$75/$100/$200/$350. Paragraph VI has separate 65 mph and 70 mph road tiers. The statute explicitly adds a penalty assessment; these are not payable totals.

sources.title: New Hampshire General Court · RSA 236:130
sources.reviewNote: Highway-surveillance prohibition contains exceptions and provisions effective September 17, 2026. This review does not turn all roadside cameras into violation-enforcement cameras or claim a universal camera ban.

sources.title: Massachusetts Legislature · Chapter 90 §20
sources.reviewNote: Speeding minimum $50 plus $10 per mph exceeding 10 mph over. Separately provides a $50 speeding surcharge and a $5 motor-vehicle surcharge; these are explicitly excluded from the displayed base minimum. Commercial-load and license consequences differ.

sources.title: Rhode Island Legislature · §31-41.1-4
sources.reviewNote: First-offense schedule lists $95 for 1–10 mph over and a $205 minimum at 11 mph over, with $10 per additional mph. Additional judicial/repeat consequences are not folded into a fixed ticket total; technology surcharge is separate.

sources.title: Rhode Island Legislature · §31-41.3-15
sources.reviewNote: School-zone camera penalty $50 per offense; new-system first 30 days require warnings. Not a moving violation for driving-record purposes. This review models the penalty for an established qualifying program violation, not all program operating conditions.

sources.title: Connecticut General Assembly · §§14-307b–14-307c
sources.reviewNote: Municipal speed-camera violations require 10+ mph over, local ordinance and DOT-approved locations. Caps are $50 first/$75 subsequent within one year; a separate electronic-processing fee may be up to $15. First 30 days at a new location require warnings.

sources.title: Connecticut General Assembly · §13a-263
sources.reviewNote: 10+ mph over in an operational work zone: first written warning; second/subsequent within one year $75. At 85 mph or more the fine is $75 even for a first offense. An officer citation for the same violation changes owner liability.

sources.title: Connecticut DOT · Current Know the Zone FAQ
sources.reviewNote: 2026 program restarted with warnings through July 5 and citations from July 6. Work-zone posted limits must be 45 mph or greater; current FAQ corroborates §13a-263 first warning/$75 subsequent and 85 mph rule.

sources.title: Connecticut General Assembly · 2026 Supplement §14-219
sources.reviewNote: §14-219(c): ordinary passenger-vehicle speeding over 70 through 85 mph on multi-lane limited-access highways, or over 60 through 85 on other highways, carries $100–$150. Lower speeds, trucks, younger drivers, special zones and reckless-driving charges require separate assessment.

sources.title: Delaware General Assembly · 21 Del.C. §4169(c)
sources.reviewNote: First base $20/subsequent within 24 months $25. Add per mph over: 6–15: $1/$2; 16–19: $2/$3; 20+: $3/$4. Paragraph (4) specifically says second offense for the higher repeat rate; this calculator withholds third+ scenarios.

sources.title: Delaware General Assembly · 21 Del.C. §4170A
sources.reviewNote: Authorized work-zone and specified residence-district systems, 11+ mph over. Civil penalty follows §4169(c). Work-zone assessments and conditional hearing costs are additional; this does not establish an active deployment. Statutory page carries a June 30, 2028 sunset.

sources.title: North Carolina General Assembly · G.S. 20-141
sources.reviewNote: More than 15 mph over or over 80 mph is a Class 3 misdemeanor. A qualifying work-zone speeding violation adds $250 where required penalty signs are posted. Other charges and license action are separate.

sources.title: North Carolina General Assembly · G.S. 20-176
sources.reviewNote: Unless a specific penalty otherwise applies, an Article infraction may carry a penalty not exceeding $100. This is a ceiling for the modeled infraction, not a fixed or payable fine.

sources.title: South Carolina Legislature · §56-5-1520(G)
sources.reviewNote: First-offense ranges: 1–10 over $15–$25; more than 10 but less than 15 $25–$50; more than 15 but less than 25 $50–$75; more than 25 $75–$200 or possible imprisonment. The exact 15/25 boundaries are withheld because the published wording leaves interpretation/charge selection unresolved.

sources.title: South Carolina Legislature · §56-7-35
sources.reviewNote: Traffic-stop, photographic-evidence and citation restrictions apply to speeding/signal tickets, with statutory exceptions. Toll and school-bus enforcement must not be represented as generic automated speeding-camera authority.

sources.title: Georgia Governor · Signed 2026 HB 651, §8
sources.reviewNote: Signed act retains $75 first/$125 later school-zone camera penalties and initial 30-day warnings. §14 makes most provisions effective July 1, 2026; §§2 and 9 start July 1, 2027. Future referendum provisions are not applied to the November 2026 calculation. Processing charges are excluded.

sources.title: Georgia Governor · Signed 2026 HB 1161
sources.reviewNote: Companion act changes school-zone device permitting and signs; ordinary provisions effective July 1, 2026, with §5 effective July 1, 2027. The calculation does not presume a permitted, operational school-zone installation or model all schedule/permit conditions.

sources.title: Florida Legislature · 2026 §318.18
sources.reviewNote: Officer base schedule: 1–5 over warning, 6–9 $25, 10–14 $100, 15–19 $150, 20–29 $175. 30+ involves mandatory-hearing rules and is withheld. Posted school and qualifying staffed/signed construction zones have special amounts/doubling. School-camera fine is separately $100 under (3)(d).

sources.title: Florida Legislature · 2026 §316.1896
sources.reviewNote: Local school-zone speed detection applies to more than 10 mph over in the specified school-session/breakfast/opening/closing windows. Warning-period and local authorization prerequisites apply; these conditions are not established by a map marker.

sources.title: Texas Legislature · Transportation §§542.401–542.404
sources.reviewNote: General misdemeanor base fine where no other penalty is provided: $1–$200. Qualifying signed work zones with workers present and notation on the notice double minimum/maximum. Separate $3 and $50 state traffic fine provisions and court costs are excluded from the base comparison. The $50 provision includes a September 1, 2025 amendment.

sources.title: Texas Legislature · Transportation §542.2035
sources.reviewNote: A municipality may not implement or operate the defined automated traffic control system on streets/highways under its jurisdiction to enforce posted speed limits. This is a scoped municipal restriction, not proof that there are no traffic, toll, plate-reader or officer-operated cameras.

sources.title: California Superior Court, Lassen · 2026 Uniform Bail and Penalty Schedule
sources.reviewNote: 2026 ordinary speed-chart base amounts are $35 (1–15 over), $70 (16–25), $100 (26+). The court schedule shows much higher totals after assessments; no county-specific payable total is generalized statewide. Special zones, prior enhancements and speeds over 100 are excluded.

sources.title: DC Office of Documents · Adopted 18 DCMR §2600, R0056041
sources.reviewNote: Downloaded the adopted rule file through its public View text action and checked the August 7, 2026 text: 1–10 over $50; 11–15 $100; 16–20 $150; 21–25 $200; 26+ controlled-access $400/other roads $500. This resolves the prior adopted-text hold.

sources.title: DC DOT · Speeding Laws, Fines and Safety Tips
sources.reviewNote: Agency states automated-photo fines are the same as officer-issued speeding fines. School/work-zone moving fines double; those special-zone calculations remain withheld pending full conditions review.

rules.title: Work-zone camera
rules.scope: Eligible operational NY work-zone program; not every construction project.
rules.notes: Prior offenses are counted within the applicable 18-month period. Workers, signs, program operation and the recorded violation must satisfy program requirements.
rules.excludes: Late/default fees, court costs, surcharges, other charges, insurance changes and nonmonetary consequences are not totaled. Local reductions or payment alternatives may apply.

rules.title: NYC school-zone camera
rules.scope: New York City only; not a statewide school-camera rate.
rules.notes: This is a statutory cap, not a payable-total prediction. Camera program conditions are separate from officer-issued school-zone citations.
rules.excludes: Late/default fees, court costs, surcharges, other charges, insurance changes and nonmonetary consequences are not totaled. Local reductions or payment alternatives may apply.

rules.title: Officer-issued speeding citation
rules.scope: VTL §1180(h)(1), (3) and (5); passenger-vehicle scenario.
rules.notes: Correct charging subsection matters. School-zone, hazardous-material and defective commercial-vehicle cases are excluded. Possible imprisonment and license consequences are not priced.
rules.excludes: Late/default fees, court costs, surcharges, other charges, insurance changes and nonmonetary consequences are not totaled. Local reductions or payment alternatives may apply.

rules.title: Work-zone camera
rules.program: PA active work-zone speed safety cameras
rules.scope: Eligible active, operating work-zone system.
rules.notes: First warning and the subsequent 15-day condition matter. No operating-record points under this civil program.
rules.excludes: Late/default fees, court costs, surcharges, other charges, insurance changes and nonmonetary consequences are not totaled. Local reductions or payment alternatives may apply.

rules.title: Officer-issued speeding citation
rules.scope: Ordinary speeding; conditional doubling in staffed, officially signed active work zones.
rules.notes: The fine is only one portion of a payable ticket. License suspension, points, safe-speed, reckless and injury charges require separate assessment.
rules.excludes: Late/default fees, court costs, surcharges, other charges, insurance changes and nonmonetary consequences are not totaled. Local reductions or payment alternatives may apply.

rules.title: Work-zone camera
rules.scope: Transportation §21-810 only; not local school/residential/I-83 camera programs.
rules.notes: Worker presence doubles the applicable tier. A police citation for the same violation changes camera liability. No license points under this civil provision.
rules.excludes: Late/default fees, court costs, surcharges, other charges, insurance changes and nonmonetary consequences are not totaled. Local reductions or payment alternatives may apply.

rules.title: Mailed speed-camera notice
rules.scope: This calculator models eligible work and school zones only, not every category authorized by the statute.
rules.notes: Shows the statutory cap; the actual local rate may be lower. Work-zone camera liability requires workers present. No driving-record conviction for a qualifying mailed notice.
rules.excludes: Late/default fees, court costs, surcharges, other charges, insurance changes and nonmonetary consequences are not totaled. Local reductions or payment alternatives may apply.

rules.title: Officer-issued speeding citation
rules.scope: Prepayable ordinary and specified school/work-zone offenses.
rules.notes: Reckless-driving thresholds stop the routine estimate. Prepayment availability, charging section, court costs and special residential-zone rules need separate checking.
rules.excludes: Late/default fees, court costs, surcharges, other charges, insurance changes and nonmonetary consequences are not totaled. Local reductions or payment alternatives may apply.

rules.title: Local pilot speed camera
rules.scope: Designated pilot jurisdictions: Los Angeles, San Jose, Oakland, Glendale, Long Beach, and the City and County of San Francisco. Eligible local streets only.
rules.notes: Not a nationwide or statewide highway program. No assumption that a jurisdiction has activated cameras. First 60 days at a new location require warnings; first vehicle violation at 11–15 mph over is also a warning. Income-based reductions are not calculated.
rules.excludes: Late/default fees, court costs, surcharges, other charges, insurance changes and nonmonetary consequences are not totaled. Local reductions or payment alternatives may apply.

rules.title: Interstate statutory minimum
rules.scope: Maine Turnpike or interstate; less than 30 mph over.
rules.notes: Displayed amount is a statutory minimum. The court fine schedule can require a higher amount; this is not an exact or average ticket.
rules.basis: Statutory base minimum; upper amount not established
rules.excludes: Court costs, assessments, surcharges, late/default fees, other charges, insurance changes and nonmonetary consequences are not totaled. Local reductions or payment alternatives may apply.

rules.title: Officer-issued speeding citation
rules.scope: Ordinary RSA 265:60 road context; separate 65/70 mph maximums.
rules.notes: Required penalty assessment is additional. School, work and specially altered speed-zone charges are not calculated.
rules.basis: Base fine; not the ticket total
rules.excludes: Court costs, assessments, surcharges, late/default fees, other charges, insurance changes and nonmonetary consequences are not totaled. Local reductions or payment alternatives may apply.

rules.title: Officer-issued speeding minimum
rules.scope: Ordinary adult passenger-vehicle speeding under the specified sections.
rules.notes: Statutory minimum only. The separate $50 speeding surcharge and $5 motor-vehicle surcharge are not included. Special zones, junior operators and commercial cases need separate assessment.
rules.basis: Statutory base minimum; excludes $55 in identified surcharges
rules.excludes: Court costs, assessments, surcharges, late/default fees, other charges, insurance changes and nonmonetary consequences are not totaled. Local reductions or payment alternatives may apply.

rules.scope: First offense in ordinary road context.
rules.notes: Higher-speed result is a published minimum rather than a complete judicial fine. Repeat-offense enhancements, judicial consequences and the technology surcharge are not totaled.
rules.basis: Base fine; not the ticket total
rules.excludes: Court costs, assessments, surcharges, late/default fees, other charges, insurance changes and nonmonetary consequences are not totaled. Local reductions or payment alternatives may apply.

rules.title: School-zone camera penalty
rules.scope: An established qualifying violation of the authorized school-zone program.
rules.notes: New-location initial 30-day warnings and program eligibility must be checked. This record models the penalty, not every operating condition or a statewide deployment map.
rules.excludes: Court costs, assessments, surcharges, late/default fees, other charges, insurance changes and nonmonetary consequences are not totaled. Local reductions or payment alternatives may apply.

rules.title: Municipal speed-camera cap
rules.scope: DOT-approved local ordinance program; not the CTDOT highway work-zone program.
rules.notes: First/$75 repeat caps differ from an exact local ordinance rate. Repeat window is one year; possible $15 processing fee is excluded. First 30 days at a location require warnings.
rules.excludes: Court costs, assessments, surcharges, late/default fees, other charges, insurance changes and nonmonetary consequences are not totaled. Local reductions or payment alternatives may apply.

rules.title: Highway work-zone camera
rules.scope: Operational CTDOT work-zone system; posted limit at least 45 mph.
rules.notes: First warning; $75 second/subsequent within one year. At 85 mph or more, $75 even for first offense. Current 2026 fines began July 6.
rules.excludes: Court costs, assessments, surcharges, late/default fees, other charges, insurance changes and nonmonetary consequences are not totaled. Local reductions or payment alternatives may apply.

rules.scope: Ordinary passenger vehicle: >70 through 85 on multi-lane limited-access roads; >60 through 85 elsewhere.
rules.notes: Lower speeds, special zones, trucks, junior-driver and reckless cases are not estimated.
rules.basis: Base fine; not the ticket total
rules.excludes: Court costs, assessments, surcharges, late/default fees, other charges, insurance changes and nonmonetary consequences are not totaled. Local reductions or payment alternatives may apply.

rules.title: Officer-issued speeding base
rules.scope: Ordinary road; first or second qualifying offense.
rules.notes: Repeat window is 24 months. Third+ scenarios are withheld due to wording in the high-speed repeat tier. Assessments and other charges are excluded.
rules.basis: Base fine; not the ticket total
rules.excludes: Court costs, assessments, surcharges, late/default fees, other charges, insurance changes and nonmonetary consequences are not totaled. Local reductions or payment alternatives may apply.

rules.scope: Authorized work-zone or specified residence-district system; 11+ mph over.
rules.notes: Uses the statutory base schedule only. Required work-zone assessments and conditional hearing costs are not included. No active-device claim is made.
rules.excludes: Court costs, assessments, surcharges, late/default fees, other charges, insurance changes and nonmonetary consequences are not totaled. Local reductions or payment alternatives may apply.

rules.scope: Modeled ordinary infraction, with optional qualifying signed work-zone addition.
rules.notes: More than 15 mph over or actual speed over 80 mph suppresses the routine infraction estimate. Required penalty signs govern the $250 work-zone addition.
rules.basis: Base fine; not the ticket total
rules.excludes: Court costs, assessments, surcharges, late/default fees, other charges, insurance changes and nonmonetary consequences are not totaled. Local reductions or payment alternatives may apply.

rules.title: First-offense speeding range
rules.scope: First offense, ordinary road context.
rules.notes: Published statutory wording requires review at exactly 15 or 25 mph over; no value is guessed there. Potential imprisonment above 25 over is not priced.
rules.basis: Base fine; not the ticket total
rules.excludes: Court costs, assessments, surcharges, late/default fees, other charges, insurance changes and nonmonetary consequences are not totaled. Local reductions or payment alternatives may apply.

rules.excludes: Court costs, assessments, surcharges, late/default fees, other charges, insurance changes and nonmonetary consequences are not totaled. Local reductions or payment alternatives may apply.

rules.excludes: Court costs, assessments, surcharges, late/default fees, other charges, insurance changes and nonmonetary consequences are not totaled. Local reductions or payment alternatives may apply.

rules.title: Officer-issued speeding base
rules.scope: Ordinary or qualifying school/work-zone context; speeds below the mandatory-hearing range.

rules.basis: Base fine; not the ticket total

holds.reason: Current monetary schedule and present camera authority require review; dated 2021 schedule and expired pilot are not treated as current penalties.

cameraPolicies.summary: Maine restricts camera-based enforcement under §2117, with school-bus and toll exceptions. A traffic-monitoring camera does not establish speed-ticket authority.
Highway surveillance is restricted with exceptions and September 2026 amendments. No generic speed-camera monetary rule is published from this review.
Texas prohibits the defined municipal automated speed-control systems under §542.2035. This does not remove officer enforcement or traffic/toll monitoring.
Speeding-ticket photographic-evidence/traffic-stop restrictions apply, with statutory exceptions. No generic automated speed-camera fine is published.
